standard_prerequisites.name: Transport along a pair path
standard_prerequisites.statement: The transport of an element of a fibre of the uncurried family along a pair path is computed by a coherence path together with the transport in the second component.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the left-hand function compared in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence and the action of a dependent function on a path
standard_prerequisites.statement: Univalence turns an equivalence between types into an identification of them, and the action of a dependent function on a path computes the transport of its values.
standard_prerequisites.use: They produce the equivalence on the right of the statement and justify the second step of the composite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A statement about an arbitrary identification can be proved by proving the case of reflexivity.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the entire proof: after the reduction both compared functions are the identity.

core_obligations: Read the two functions being compared: the transport along the pair path in the uncurried family, and the equivalence obtained by univalence from the composite of the two displayed transports (source lines 1712-1723).
Reduce the comparison by path induction to the case where the two points coincide and the identification is reflexivity (source line 1725).
Observe that in that case both functions are the identity, which proves the comparison (source line 1725).

proof_roadmap.step: The statement compares a transport along a pair path with a univalent composite.
Path induction reduces the comparison to the reflexivity case, where both functions are the identity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 1712-1723: for a doubly dependent family and a pair path, the transport in the uncurried family is the equivalence obtained by univalence from the composite of two transports. The proof (source lines 1724-1726) is a single path induction, but it is the complete argument for this comparison rather than a pointer to another result: after the induction both compared functions reduce to the identity, because the coherence path and both transports become reflexivity. What the card counts is the comparison itself, whose content lies in the statement: identifying the two transports, exhibiting the coherence path and invoking the action of the dependent function on the identification. The reduction step is recorded verbatim and the statement carries the substance.
